ソースカツ丼.summary: A katsudon called the soul food of Fukui. Pork pounded thin is coated in fine breadcrumbs, fried, dipped in a special Worcestershire-based sauce and laid over rice. There is no egg, so you can enjoy the crisp cutlet and the aroma of the sauce. It is said to have been born in Tokyo in the Taisho era and spread after it reached Fukui. You can try it at a long-established Western-style restaurant in Fukui City and at many other places in the prefecture. Many shops serve about three cutlets per bowl.

shops.name: Europe-ken Sohonten
shops.query: ヨーロッパ軒 総本店 福井
shops.comment: The originator of sauce katsudon. Weekend lines are common.

shops.name: Tsuruga Europe-ken
shops.query: 敦賀ヨーロッパ軒 本店
shops.comment: A sauce katsudon favorite in Tsuruga.

ボルガライス.summary: A local dish from Echizen City, formerly Takefu. An omelette over rice is topped with a pork cutlet and covered with demi-glace or another sauce, making a very filling Western-style meal. One theory links the name to the Volga River in Russia, but nobody really knows. The combination of fluffy egg, ketchup rice and crispy cutlet is loved by children and adults alike. You can find it at Western-style restaurants and cafes in Echizen City, and each shop uses a different sauce. Come hungry.

shops.name: Yokogawa Bunten
shops.query: ヨコガワ分店 越前市
shops.comment: The best-known volga rice shop in Takefu, inside the Sosha Daijingu grounds.
shops.access: About 11 min walk from Takefu Station

shops.name: Cafe de Imari
shops.query: カフェ・ド・伊万里 越前市
shops.comment: An Echizen City café serving volga rice.

油揚げステーキ.summary: Fukui is said to be among the top prefectures in Japan for eating fried tofu. Large, thick pieces are grilled until golden, topped with grated daikon, green onion and bonito flakes, and drizzled with soy sauce. Crisp and fragrant outside and fluffy inside, it is full of juicy soybean flavor. One reason it is so popular is that fried tofu has long been used in vegetarian dishes for Hoonko, a Buddhist memorial service of the Jodo Shinshu sect. It goes well with both rice and drinks.

shops.name: Taniguchiya
shops.query: 谷口屋 竹田 油揚げ
shops.comment: Eat the huge Takeda aburaage fresh from the fryer.

shops.name: Fukui Shoku no Kuni 291 (Ginza)
shops.query: ふくい食の國291 銀座
shops.comment: Fukui's antenna shop in Ginza, Tokyo, with Taniguchiya aburaage daily.

おろしそば.summary: The classic way to eat Echizen soba: cold buckwheat noodles topped with spicy grated daikon and a flavorful dashi-based sauce. The sharp bite of the daikon goes perfectly with the aroma of the soba, making it light and easy to eat. Some shops pour the daikon juice over the noodles, while others mix it into a dipping sauce, so styles vary. Bonito flakes and green onion are common toppings. There are many Echizen soba shops throughout the prefecture. It is a Fukui specialty you should not miss.

shops.name: Miyoshiya
shops.query: 越前そば 見吉屋 福井
shops.comment: A 90-year-old backstreet favorite in Fukui City.

shops.name: Moriroku
shops.query: 手打そば 森六 越前市
shops.comment: Founded in the Meiji era. Closes when the soba runs out.

へしこ.summary: A traditional preserved food of the Wakasa area: fish such as mackerel is salted, then packed in rice bran and aged for a long time. The fish's umami becomes concentrated, with saltiness and the distinctive aroma of rice bran. The standard way is to slice it thin, grill it lightly, and serve it with sake or rice. In ochazuke, with tea poured over rice, the saltiness softens and it becomes easy to eat. It has long been made in Wakasa fishing villages and is sold at souvenir shops and roadside stations. It is a popular drinking snack.

shops.name: Tamuracho
shops.query: 田村長 小浜
shops.comment: A seafood shop founded in the Edo period, about 200 years old.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Wakasa Obama
shops.query: 道の駅 若狭おばま
shops.comment: A roadside station with several kinds of heshiko.

越前ガニ.summary: Male snow crab landed at ports in Fukui, called the king of winter delicacies. A yellow tag is attached as a mark of quality. The shells are packed with sweet meat and rich crab miso. You can enjoy it boiled, grilled, as sashimi or in a hot pot. The season is limited to winter, when many visitors come to hot spring inns along the Echizen Coast just for crab dishes. It is one of the greatest pleasures of a winter trip to Fukui. Prices vary widely by size and quality.
越前ガニ.area: Echizen Coast (Echizen Town, Sakai and around)

shops.name: Echizen Kani no Bo
shops.query: 越前蟹の坊 三国
shops.comment: An Echizen crab restaurant run by a Meiji-era inn.

shops.name: Mikuni Inkyojo
shops.query: みくに隠居処 越前がに
shops.comment: One of the few places handling imperial-presentation crab.

shops.name: Araya
shops.query: 三国温泉 あらや 越前ガニ
shops.comment: An inn near Tojinbo, with a restaurant.

焼き鯖寿司.summary: Pressed sushi made of grilled fatty mackerel laid over vinegared rice. Grilling brings out the mackerel's aroma and flavor, so even people who dislike raw mackerel find it easy to eat. The Wakasa area thrived on mackerel and is known as the start of the Saba Kaido, the mackerel road to Kyoto. Grilled mackerel sushi is also popular as a station bento and an airport specialty. Warm it slightly and the fat melts, making it even tastier. It is sold at souvenir shops and stations in Obama and the Wakasa area.

shops.name: Echizen Mikuni Minatoya
shops.query: 越前三國湊屋
shops.comment: The shop that created and named yaki-saba sushi. Takeout only.

shops.name: Fukui Station souvenir shops
shops.query: 福井駅 焼き鯖寿司
shops.comment: Several makers' yaki-saba sushi are sold in the station.

丸焼き鯖.summary: A Wakasa specialty: a whole mackerel skewered on bamboo and slowly grilled over charcoal. Also called hamayaki saba, it offers fragrant grilled skin and plump, fatty flesh. You can eat it with ginger and soy sauce or flake it into mackerel rice. The Wakasa area is said to have had a custom of eating it during the rice-planting season. Fish shops and markets in Obama sell it, and some serve it freshly grilled. Biting straight into it is the local way.

shops.name: Kutsukiya
shops.query: 朽木屋 小浜 浜焼き鯖
shops.comment: A mackerel specialist from the Edo period; set meals upstairs on weekends.

shops.name: Wakasa Obama Osakana Center
shops.query: 若狭小浜お魚センター
shops.comment: A market of Obama seafood.

羽二重餅.summary: Fukui's most famous sweet, made by kneading glutinous rice flour with sugar and starch syrup into a soft, smooth confection. It is named after habutae, a fine silk fabric produced in Fukui, for its thin, silky feel. In the mouth it is meltingly soft with an elegant, gentle sweetness. There are many variations, such as ones with soybean flour or red bean paste. It is widely sold at Fukui Station and souvenir shops in the prefecture. It is so thin and soft that people tear it off with their fingers.

shops.name: Matsuokaken
shops.query: 羽二重餅總本舗 松岡軒 本店
shops.comment: Founded in the Meiji era, where habutae mochi began. With a café.

shops.name: Matsuokaken Kurufu Fukui Station
shops.query: くるふ福井駅 松岡軒
shops.comment: Buy it inside Fukui Station.

水ようかん.summary: In Fukui, people have a custom of eating mizu yokan, a soft red bean jelly, in winter. Eating cold mizu yokan while sitting at a kotatsu heated table is a winter pleasure here. It usually comes poured into a flat paper box and is cut with the small wooden spatula provided. Most are made with brown sugar, lightly sweet and smooth going down. In winter, supermarkets and confectioners in the prefecture stock plenty of it. It is so light that some people finish a whole box in one go.

shops.name: Egawa
shops.query: えがわ 水羊かん 福井
shops.comment: A mizu-yokan shop open only in winter (Nov–Mar), closed over New Year.

shops.name: Fukui Station souvenir shops
shops.query: 福井駅 水ようかん
shops.comment: In winter, several makers' mizu-yokan are sold in the station.

五月ヶ瀬.summary: A baked sweet packed with peanuts, made by a long-established Fukui confectioner. A dough of flour, eggs and sugar is generously mixed with roasted peanuts and baked until crunchy. The toasty peanuts and gentle sweetness make it hard to stop eating. It is a long-loved classic souvenir of Fukui, sold at Fukui Station and souvenir shops in the prefecture. Individually wrapped pieces make it easy to share. It also goes well with coffee or tea.

shops.name: Satsukigase Harue Main Store
shops.query: 五月ヶ瀬 春江総本店
shops.comment: The main store of Satsukigase.

shops.name: Kurufu Fukui Station
shops.query: くるふ福井駅 五月ヶ瀬
shops.comment: Fukui Station's souvenir area.
